frontier_question: Why did OpenAI release GPT-5 in August 2025, and what did it change about how the company sells its models?

chunks.content: OpenAI released GPT-5 (with GPT-5 mini) on 2025-08-07, available to free users immediately — a deliberate shift to give-away-the-frontier pricing. GPT-5 retired the separate o-series products: o3, o4-mini, o3-mini and o3-pro were folded into GPT-5's internal "reasoning modes"; OpenAI's pitch was "GPT-5 is not a 'reasoning model'; it's a model that thinks" — one model, no model picker. The features: a 5-million-token context window, native image generation built in (no separate image model), deep research integrated, and file upload and web search out of the box. Pricing: free on the free tier; Plus $20/month (unlimited GPT-5); Pro $200/month; API pricing $1.25 / $10 per million tokens for GPT-5 and $0.25 / $2 for GPT-5 mini. GPT-5 scored about 78.6% on SWE-bench Verified, with GPT-5 mini close behind — both at a fraction of the o-series prices. The launch consolidated OpenAI's strategy around one unified model plus aggressive free-tier distribution: the reasoning-vs-non-reasoning split ended, price collapsed, and the competitive battleground moved from benchmark demos to default agency — models that act, not models that answer.

prior_gap_texts: OpenAI released GPT-5 on August 7, 2025 [Source: ev-1] to consolidate its strategy around a single unified model and shift the competitive focus from benchmark demonstrations to "default agency"—models that act rather than just answer [Source: ev-1].

This release marked a deliberate strategic pivot toward aggressive free-tier distribution by making the frontier model available immediately to free users, effectively adopting a "give-away-the-frontier" pricing approach [Source: ev-1].

The launch fundamentally changed how OpenAI sells its models in several key ways:
*   **Unified Model Architecture:** It ended the split between reasoning and non-reasoning products. [Source: ev-1]

The separate o-series (o3, o4-mini, o3-mini, and o3-pro) were retired and folded into GPT-5's internal "reasoning modes," eliminating the need for customers to pick different models for different tasks [Source: ev-1].

While Pro remains at $200/month and Plus at $20/month, API pricing was set at $1.25 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens for GPT-5, with GPT-5 mini available at $0.25/$2 [Source: ev-1].
These prices are described as a fraction of what the o-series cost [Source: ev-1].

*   **Feature Integration:** The model launched with an expanded 5-million-token context window, native image generation (removing the need for a separate image model), integrated deep research capabilities, and built-in file upload and web search features [Source: ev-1].
Despite these changes in distribution and pricing, GPT-5 maintained high performance, scoring approximately 78.6% on SWE-bench Verified [Source: ev-1].
